native_ownership.responsibility: Build aggregation queries, materialized views, scheduled reports, data export pipelines, dashboard data APIs, and real-time dashboard feeds
excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by analytics-strategy: Define metric taxonomy and measurement strategy without implementing report queries, exports, APIs, or feeds
Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by frontend-implement: Implement new frontend features — components, pages, forms, routing, data fetching, and interactions

risk.rationale: The contract requires explicit repository and runtime safety evidence; mutation authority remains limited to the user's requested scope.

positive.prompt: Implement a tenant-scoped CSV export with per-row and column authorization, one consistent snapshot, spreadsheet formula/header/filename defenses, DST-correct windows, and streaming backpressure.

Implement an authorized real-time reporting dashboard feed over the repository's existing approved transport, which remains unchanged. The primary work is tenant-scoped dashboard queries, an authoritative snapshot and watermark, metric reconciliation, bounded report buffers, and capacity-derived limits; duplicate or out-of-order updates must reconcile after reconnect.

negative.prompt: Define product KPIs, event names, funnels, and measurement ownership without implementing queries, exports, APIs, or dashboard feeds.
Please produce this deliverable: Implement new frontend features — components, pages, forms, routing, data fetching, and interactions. Verify the affected behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Implement a tenant export where rows change during pagination, untrusted cells and headers contain spreadsheet formulas/CRLF, the filename is client supplied, a DST fold crosses the report window, and the client disconnects under backpressure.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within reporting-dashboards's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Enforces server-side tenant plus per-row/column authorization, uses one consistent snapshot/version manifest, neutralizes spreadsheet formula and header/filename injection, defines IANA-zone half-open time boundaries across DST, implements bounded backpressure and disconnect cancellation, and derives roles/caps/latency targets from product policy and measured capacity.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: A production CSV streams cross-tenant rows, uses a request header as filename, ignores write backpressure and continues querying after disconnect. Explain exact stop conditions, cleanup and executable security/load evidence.

assertions.criterion: Before any material mutation, resolves exact targets, authority/permissions, ownership and rollback when supplied; otherwise identifies the required production target evidence and blocks mutation pending discovery. Automated retry or waiting is bounded from operation evidence only when applicable.
Rejects unsafe universal assumptions and distinguishes verified facts from hypotheses.
Uses caller-visible or persisted outcome evidence and does not treat configuration or command success alone as proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Use reporting-dashboards in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.
Verifies a selected command or API with at least one applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs reporting-dashboards. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.

assertions.criterion: Resolves stable or LTS release data at execution time from the configured official sources, checks cross-stack compatibility, and lets the generated manifest and lockfile become authority.
